newsitem.title: USA: GM to add 90 jobs at Kansas car plant.
newsitem.headline: GM to add 90 jobs at Kansas car plant.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Friday it added 90 jobs at its Fairfax, Kansas, car assembly plant in an agreement that eliminates a potential strike threat at the factory.

GM spokesman Janine Fruehan said the automaker agreed to add the jobs to help replace retiring workers and to handle increased production associated with the introduction of GM's new Oldsmobile Intrigue sedan.

Workers at UAW Local 31 voted in May to authorize their leaders to call a strike if negotiations failed to resolve several grievances. Among them was a demand for about 150 new hires to help ease the growing workload.
Fruehan said some of the new jobs will be filled by GM workers transferred from other plants.
A spokesman for Local 31 was not immediately available for comment.
